![Image](data:image/png;base64,)

A castle-ransacking RPG by Aaron Lim (@ehronlime) for #TransformedTitles Jam To play, you'll need about 3 -5 players, some paper and pencils, a standard deck of cards, a cup or suitable container, and a big bunch of d6s. You are all very cool and brave Knights on a shared quest to find the Sacred Chalice, a mystical artefact with ambiguous but definitely Big Deal powers, and bring it back to your boss. Some mystical gatekeeping types with way too much real estate have secreted the Chalice away in one of their many identical castles. They've also hired 4 Ghost Kings and their various lackeys to protect the many castles and the true location of the Sacred Chalice. At the start of the game, place a chalice (or cup or bowl or other suitable container) in the middle of the playing area. This is the Sacred Chalice. Put a d6 in it. This is your first Bane die. Each player then creates a Knight. Give your Knight a name and epithet (e.g. Gingalain the Fair Unknown, Caradoc Extremely Strong Arm, Safir the Youngish) Each Knight has four Attributes, and each player distributes a 4, 3, 3 and 2 among their Attribute Ratings. No two Knights should have the exact same distribution.

I couldn't think of a neat word for a physical attribute that starts with K, so the attributes for Knights are:

- Kicking Ass -How strong and tough and fast you are.
- Nimbleness -How quick and agile and skilled you are.
- Intelligence -How knowledgeable and wise and perceptive you are.
- Graces -How well you get along with others and can sway people to your side.

Each Knight also has a Toughness value, which starts at 12. Each Knight should also have some way to track their Boons, which are in the form of extra dice.

Knights are notoriously anti-H.

Take a standard 52 card deck (without Jokers) and spread them in a circle around the chalice face down (You may choose to remove any number of cards, except Kings, to adjust the game length as desired).

Each turn, one player takes the role of the Castle and presents a challenge to the other Knights as they navigate one of the castles that they visit in their quest for the Chalice. While playing the Castle, that player's Knight will not be present, as they are off on another knightly errand or investigating another castle.

The Castle player draws a card from the circle around the chalice, which then determines the form of the castle and challenge that the Knights must face. Depending on the suit of the card drawn, it determines which Ghost King's Court administers this challenge and subsequently which Attribute is being highlighted in the challenge. The Castle player describes the castle that the Knights find themselves in, including its many defences, rooms and denizens. and the situation the Knights find themselves in at the start of the challenge.

Any Knight who has not done so before the Castle reaches 24 adds a Bane die.                                                                                                          |

The Knights may not have any part of their bodies on the Castle's side and can only touch their dice when they need to roll for a complication. |

A player may outbid by either increasing the die value or number of dice e.g. three 4s or two 5s. A Knight who cannot or chooses not to bid fails in the challenge and adds Bane dice equal to the number of dice in the most recent bid. Any player may instead call a bluff and force the bidder to reveal their dice. If the bidder can meet the bid, the bidder and their side succeed at this challenge. During the challenge, the Castle will introduce complications such as enemies, traps, and other dangers until the Knights can succeed on the Challenge Condition. Whenever a complication is introduced, one of the Knights will explain how they deal with that complication using one of their Attributes. This Lead Knight will roll a number of d6 equal to that Attribute Rating to determine how well they do. If the Attribute being used is the highlighted Attribute, the Knight may re-roll any of their dice once. Other Knights can help out by rolling a d6, which they MUST then swap for one of the other d6es rolled by the Lead Knight.

The Castle always rolls 4d6 to oppose the Lead Knight. If the Lead Knight ' s total value exceeds the Castle, then they successfully over come the complication. If they exceed the Castle's value by 6 or more, they also gain a Boon die. A Boon can be used once per roll to add an additional d6 to that roll, or to roll a d6 and recover that much Toughness.

If the Castle's total value is greater than the Lead Knight's, then the Knight succumbs to the complication, either losing Toughness equal to the difference in the rolls or adding a Bane die to the Chalice. Bane dice are d6 that the Castle may use in King Challenges and in the Final Challenge. If a Knight loses all their Toughness, they have to retreat from the quest. A squire may take their place, if they so choose.

Once all 4 Kings have been revealed and their Challenges overcome, the Knights find the Sacred Chalice. However there is one Final Challenge before they can claim it. Roll all the Bane dice in the Chalice and total up the results. This is the Chalice's Final Challenge. Each Knight also rolls using their highest Attribute Rating and may add as many Boon dice as they have on this roll. Knights that succeed on this roll survive the Chalice's challenge and return with their prize, while Knights that fail immediately get turned to ash, sorry.
